title: Win or Come Home

source.title: Americans 'frustrated' about Iran war going into midterms as Trump admin has decision to make: GOP lawmaker
source.note: published 10-30 13:49 EDT; the 10-30 sweep (matched on 'iran', 'midterm'). Fox's station on the roster is 'RI?' — proposed, ruling owed; scored as RI on the 10-20 → 10-29 precedents, flag on the figure. Read in full via the cloud fetch on 11-01 (the 10-31 and 11-01 sweeps never reached GitHub; this is the second pass over the 10-30 queue); filed as reductions, no quotation over twelve words. Twelve body paragraphs (teasers and captions excluded from the count; the CENTCOM caption filed in the pass). One voice: a House Armed Services Republican (NC-10) to Fox News Digital, with the vice-president reported once. Chosen as the newest Fox hit on the live object still uncut in the queue; over the Kudlow page (Fox Business 10-29 — 'gasoline' once, the economy 'booming'; one Fox cut per day) and the Libertarians page (Iran once); my call

object.label: the next offensive against Iran — the force (PG01 §5, the war that made the crunch): read from the RI corner through a House Armed Services Republican on the Friday before the vote. The page's record line is the article's: 'moves are underway to give the president options if he resumes strikes' (¶2), reported beside the vice-president's 'not going to let Iran become a forever war'. The congressman answers with a binary — 'either win or come home' — and then names the steady state he would accept: 'persistent over the horizon monitoring' and strikes to 'mow the lawn every now and again' (¶8). The deal, the price and the Strait are not on the page; 'economic stability' once (¶9)

zAxis.pos: the force relents — the vote changes the course, the war ends or is declared met, and no new strike follows
zAxis.neg: it does not — options for resumed strikes are being prepared, the only stop on offer is a Congress not yet elected, and the corner's own reader describes the strike as lawn-mowing

transformNote: the shadow is the holder's office's promise — 'not going to let Iran become a forever war' (Vance, Fox town hall, reported ¶2) — the same shadow the LI corner put in a voter's mouth the same day ('he should keep his promises — no wars'). The page puts the record beside it in the same paragraph: 'moves are underway to give the president options if he resumes strikes'. The RI reader does not dispute the record; he reframes the force as a decision owed ('win or come home') and then describes the version of it that is not a forever war — monitoring plus periodic strikes — in the same breath. 'If he renews military action' (¶6) presumes the renewal; the stop asked for is Congress, from inside the majority party

log.what: cut from the 10-30 sweep on its second day as the queue (no 10-31 or 11-01 sweep on GitHub at run time — the daily slop did not land for two days). Twelve body paragraphs read in full via the cloud fetch; twelve scored (eleven inferred, one declared) and one constitutive (Vance @O, the principal — declared +0.8). Object declared on the force (PG01 §5), the A Spine (10-31) precedent from the other side of the paper: the same report ('options if he resumes strikes') from the RI corner, through a majority-party reader. My calls: Vance stationed @O as the holder's office (the 10-21 MS NOW precedent) rather than with the publication; 'mow the lawn' scored O at 28 — the force described, not framed; the two ballot lines (¶11–¶12) kept as vacancy for the page's Dia; the NC-10 line kept as T at zero (slate). One Fox cut per day; reversible

split.note: one station, one reader, two planes: the record and the mechanism at 8–30 (options underway, involve Congress, the funding arm, mow the lawn, the binary decision); the frustration and the ballot at 36–52 (frustrated, inevitable, responsible, the House majority, the direction of the country). No second chair. Harrigan runs 38 · 44 · 30 · 16 · 26 · 28 · 40 · 46 · 52 — down each time he names a mechanism, up each time he names the stakes; the article's one record line (8) is the page's floor

scoreboard.zRule: every line carries a z, inferred where implied (Sailor 2026-10-13); inferred lines are marked zInferred with a zWhy

lines.quote: the administration has a key decision to make on the future of the war; doing just enough not to lose but not enough to win is not OK
lines.note: THE DOOR: the force put as a decision owed — the lede reports the reader's binary before the record
lines.zWhy: a decision still to be made on an unfinished war is a war not relenting

lines.quote: not going to let Iran become a forever war
lines.note: constitutive — THE SHADOW, from the holder's office at a Fox town hall (reported): the force promised to relent, undated. The LI corner quoted the holder's 'no new wars' the same day. Not Dia-scored

lines.quote: officials and military sources say moves are underway to give the president options if he resumes strikes
lines.note: THE RECORD, in one reported clause — the page's lowest line; 'if he resumes' is the report Surveillance priced and MS NOW dated the same day
lines.zWhy: options being prepared for resumed strikes is the force being readied, not relenting

lines.quote: very, very frustrated that this war is not over; the administration needed to end it quickly; we are not there yet
lines.note: the reader's temperature — 'frustrated' the vehicle; the clause under it is that the war is not over
lines.zWhy: a war not over in month eight is not relenting

lines.quote: Iran can't have a nuclear weapon; the war was inevitable; the party in power is responsible for its outcome
lines.note: three frames in one paragraph — necessity, inevitability, ownership; the object inside them unmeasured
lines.zWhy: a war owned as inevitable is read as continuing until its owner ends it

lines.quote: do what it takes to either win or come home; that binary decision has to get made by this administration
lines.note: THE TITLE — the mechanism offered is a decision, with two exits and no date
lines.zWhy: a binary still to be chosen is a war still on

lines.quote: Trump needs to involve Congress if he renews military action against the Iranian regime
lines.note: THE STOP FROM THE RIGHT: Congress, asked for by a member of the majority — 'if he renews' presumes the renewal
lines.zWhy: a stop asked for before a renewal is a renewal expected

lines.quote: Congress is responsible for the funding arm; running out of money for objectives would harm our strategic interests
lines.note: the stop sized as the purse — the one instrument the reader's chamber holds
lines.zWhy: a funding arm invoked is a war being funded

lines.quote: either win, or declare the objectives largely met — with persistent over-the-horizon monitoring and mowing the lawn every now and again
lines.note: THE FORCE DESCRIBED AS MAINTENANCE: 'come home' spelled out is periodic strikes plus monitoring; the version of the force that is not a forever war, from inside the majority
lines.zWhy: a war ended by periodic strikes is a force that does not relent, by its own reader's account

lines.quote: continuing to do just enough is not OK for Americans, for the troops, for economic stability; it's time to choose
lines.note: 'economic stability' — the page's one touch on the price's side, unnamed and unsized; 'time to choose' the vehicle
lines.zWhy: a choice still owed is a war still on
